articleTitle: Adaptive Finite Element Implementation in Julia
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a simple adaptive 3D finite element code in the Julia programming language. The library was developed to build a tool for the automated creation of numerous simulations, forming a database for deep neural network training. The author aims to present Julia as an extremely useful tool for fast finite element code development.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of ceramic material extrusion
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper is focused on computer simulations related to the extrusion of ceramic material for continuous 3D printing. The aim is to optimize the process of extrusion of ceramic material using numerical simulations. These simulations are essential for understanding fluid dynamics in 3D printers, especially when working with complex materials such as ceramic clays and clays with additives. The speed at which the material is extruded is optimized. Depending on the printed model, suitable nozzle sizes and layer thicknesses are selected. Based on these computer models, a universal custom ceramic 3D printer was developed. This printer can create mechanically stable shapes and add fine details and decorative elements to final ceramic prints.

articleTitle: Application of neural networks to the identification of artificial defects using sweep-frequency eddy current testing
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article discusses the practical application of the inverse method of electromagnetic non-destructive investigation of austenitic materials. It includes the design of a robust tool for the automated localization of material defects. To identify and evaluate deep artificial defects, the sweep-frequency eddy current method with harmonic excitation is used. The objects of interest are surface electric-discharged machined notches with a defined geometry fabricated in a plate with a thickness of 30 mm. By using the designed probe combined with the frequency sweeping of eddy currents, it is possible to reliably detect artificial defects up to 24 ± 0.5 mm deep by using low-frequency excitation signals. An important fact is that the measuring probe does not have to be placed directly above the examined defect. The achieved experimental results are processed and evaluated. For this purpose, we designed and tested a simple neural network whose task is to identify defects in the material's structure and indicate the probable occurrence of defects. The network is designed to be able to locate not only visible defects but also those located inside the material.

articleTitle: Design of reconfigurable circular polarization equilateral triangular antenna without and with air gap
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative performance study of an equilateral triangular patch antenna (ETPA) with and without an additional air gap substrate. The proposed antenna covers the S-band (2.4GHz-2.5GHz) for satellite communication. The antenna consists of truncated equilateral triangular patches connected at the truncated corners by two PIN diodes to the two parasitic triangular patches. A dual circular polarization is obtained by switching the PIN diodes in ON and/or OFF state. An additional air gap is introduced between the ground and the substrate to improve the gain and the bandwidth(sparameter and axial ratio).The simulated results demonstrate a 7.76 dBic realize gain, a return loss bandwidth of 195 Mhz and axial ratio bandwidth of 51 Mhz.

articleTitle: The Application of Real-time Simulation Technology in Mongolian Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper examines the use of real-time simulation technology to optimize and enhance efficiency in Mongolia’s energy system. It explores the challenges facing Mongolia’s energy sector and how real-time simulation can help address these issues. The paper discusses the benefits, opportunities, and best practices of using real-time simulation within a power grid, as well as Mongolia's transition to advanced energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Measurement and Simulation of Radiofrequency Electromagnetic Field Exposure of a Tissue Phantom with an Implanted Pacemaker Device
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The purpose of the article is to investigate electromagnetic field exposure a person with an implanted device experiences when using a mobile phone in the DCS band. This study will involve measuring, analysing, and quantifying radiofrequency (RF) electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure to understand its impact on EMF distribution and to identify potential health risks for people with implantable devices. The measurement results are compared to simulations results of RF-EMF exposure of a two phantom models with an implantable pacemaker device with the chose the best model. Based on our experimental measurements and simulations, we found that maintaining a minimum distance of 15 cm between the mobile phone and the pacemaker is not enough to ensure patient safety.

articleTitle: Verification of the efficacy of long-term bathing in a weakly radioactive alkaline simple sulfur spring on arteriosclerosis based on the mathematical model of the development of arteriosclerosis: including verification using an improved analysis method
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The efficacy of a single bath in weakly radioactive alkaline simple sulfur springs, radioactive springs and alkaline springs on arteriosclerosis has been previously verified based on a mathematical model of the development of arteriosclerosis. On the other hand, studies have also been conducted on the efficacy of long-term bathing in weakly radioactive alkaline simple sulfur springs on arteriosclerosis and it has been found that bathing over a long period of time (about three months) is effective with more frequent bathing being even more effective in the pervious analysis. In this study, the efficacy of long-term bathing in weakly radioactive alkaline simple sulfur springs on arteriosclerosis is reverified using an improved analysis method. Based on the mathematical model of the development of arteriosclerosis, it has been revealed that keeping blood cholesterol levels low inhibits the progression of arteriosclerosis. Therefore, blood cholesterol levels are estimated using a minimally invasive skin cholesterol ester level measurement device that irradiates the skin with mid-infrared light and calculates the cholesterol ester level of the skin from the absorption spectrum intensity. In the improved analysis method, the change in the difference between the "peak" and "valley" of the cholesterol ester absorption spectrum before and after bathing is examined. The analysis revealed that after about three months of bathing, statistically significant increase of people whose cholesterol levels were improved due to decreasing the difference between the "peak" and "valley" is confirmed. This means that the efficacy of long-term bathing in weakly radioactive alkaline simple sulfur springs on arteriosclerosis has been verified.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Methods for Preparing Input Data for Neural Networks Used in Lightning Threat Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper proposes automating the process of designing lightning protection systems. The impetus for improving the efficiency of this process came from the standardization procedures contained in IEC 62305, which are rigid and sometimes lead to overestimation or underestimation of the parameters of the lightning protection system. As a result of such actions, incorrect decisions may be made regarding applying a lightning protection system with suboptimally selected parameters for the objects of interest or even its complete omission. The automation of this process is based on two paths: starting with simulations of the electric field intensity distribution around objects at risk of lightning strikes and using neural networks designed to assess the locations particularly vulnerable to lightning threats. The process involving neural networks also includes a description of data preparation based on the Ansys Maxwell environment for use in an artificial neural network (ANN) based on Matlab and the Julia environment for use in an ANN based on Darknet.

articleTitle: Multi-point algorithm for eliminating hyper-chaotic vibrations in nonlinear dynamical systems
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents an effective algorithm for stabilizing periodic orbits immersed in a strange attractor of phase trajectories, which involves small changes in selected parameters of the hyper-chaotic system at each sampling time. The applied control concept consists in modifying selected system parameters in such a way as to minimize the distance of the trajectory from a fixed point on the cross-section of the generalized Poincaré map. Using of multiple control parameters allows for the effective elimination of hyper-chaotic vibrations in complex nonlinear systems in the presence of strong disturbances and noise. The main attention has been focused on a non-autonomous hyper-chaotic system, which can be treated as representative of many advanced non-linear phenomena occurring in the real world. A characteristic property of the considered dynamical systems is the presence of at least two positive Lyapunov exponents. Such systems show very strong sensitivity to initial conditions and generate extremely complex strange attractors. The results of representative computer simulations have been analyzed and interpreted in detail.

articleTitle: Industrial energy storage system for photovoltaic and wind power systems - selected research results from the implementation of a 0.8 MWh lithium-ion energy storage system
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The growing penetration of renewable energy sources from wind and sun is a challenge to the stability of the power system. One of the more promising ways to flatten the characteristics of energy production from these sources may be battery energy storage. Lithium-ion technology is becoming more and more profitable, but its safe use must be supervised by an advanced battery management system (BMS). This is especially important in the case of large-capacity industrialscale storage systems. This article contains selected research results for this energy storage system, documenting, among other things, the energy efficiency of the nickel-manganese-cobalt and lithium-iron-phosphate type of lithium-ion technology systems and the correct operation of the complex (BMS). The results of the battery storage cooperation with a 250 kW photovoltaic power plant are presented.

articleTitle: Modeling and study of the reactive power consumption mode of an arc furnace
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A high-performance system for stabilizing the consumption mode of reactive power of an arc furnace (AF) has been developed. The system operates using the principles of thyristor control of the equivalent inductance of the throttles included in the primary circuit of the furnace transformer. The dependencies of the artificial external characteristics of the arc furnace for multicriteria optimal control of the process to stabilize the reactive power consumption mode are backgrounded. A computer model of the proposed system for reactive power optimal stabilization of the arc furnace was created. Model studies the integral indicators of dynamics and energy efficiency under regulation of random disturbances by the proposed system and a typical arc power regulator of the arc furnace. The obtained research results showed a comprehensive improvement in the quality indicators of the dynamics of reactive power stabilization and AF energy efficiency indicators.

articleTitle: TOPAS Monte Carlo and Eclipse Treatment Planning System Validation*
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Various algorithms are employed in radiotherapy (RT) to compute the dosage. The accuracy of the calculated dose in RT is crucial for ensuring agreement with the delivered dose. The objective is to prioritize the accuracy of algorithms that directly influence the clinical results of patients. We aim to compare photon beam simulation between ARIA - Eclipse TPS (Varian Medical Systems, Palo Alto, CA, USA) and TOPAS MC (Tool for Particle Simulation, Monte Carlo). We aim to incorporate Monte Carlo simulations into our teaching methodology. Therefore, we must accurately define the simulation parameters to effectively compare our findings with the clinical calculations conducted at the Department of Medical and Radiation Oncology at Zilina Hospital. Monte Carlo simulations of ionizing radiation transmission from the source to the patient provide a simplified fundamental comprehension of radiotherapy. This study presents a comparative analysis percentual depth doses. The results indicate that comparing TOPAS MC and Eclipse TPS produces positive outcomes. TOPAS MC can accurately replicate the needed scenarios, ensuring they align with clinical outcomes. The results indicate that the TOPAS MC program may be helpful in the teaching process for simulating ionizing radiation.

articleTitle: Characterization of Electromagnetic Fields in a GTEM Cell Using a KSQ1000 Comb Generator and Analysis of Comb Generator Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into the characterization of electromagnetic fields within a Gigahertz Transverse Electromagnetic cell using a commercially available KSQ1000 comb generator. The measurements provide detailed information on the field uniformity and frequency response across the cell volume. This data is crucial for ensuring the accuracy and reliability of various electromagnetic compatibility testing applications conducted within the GTEM cell. Furthermore, the paper delves into the underlying technologies employed for comb generator manufacturing, with a specific focus on Non-Linear Transmission Lines. This analysis offers valuable insights into the selection criteria for comb generators.

articleTitle: Multi-level analysis of EFT/Burst disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: EFT/Burst disturbances are one of the most influential phenomena in sensitive devices. The selection of protection measures against them is determined by its nature. Due to the complexity of these disturbances, it is worth conducting a multilevel analysis, mainly frequency analysis of the disorder under study, before developing suppression methods.This paper’s authors analysed the voltage and current waveforms recorded at the measuring station for the chosen relays and load parameters. The analysis aimed to understand the detailed characteristics of the disturbance under study and is also an introduction to developing the best possible method for selecting coupling elements. Due to assumptions, analysis was done for measured, simulated and ideal (standardised parameters) disturbances. Finally, the authors summarised the results and concluded.

articleTitle: Implementation of EMG Signals for Hand Prosthesis Control
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article presents a prototype of a hand prosthesis controlled by electromyographic (EMG) signals. The prosthetic hand, along with the forearm, was 3D printed using PETG material. An Arduino Uno microcontroller was chosen to control the servomechanisms, while a polyester braid was used to transmit movement from the servomechanisms to the fingers. The EMG signals were captured by three dry surface electrodes attached to the forearm with a strap. These signals were sent to an amplifier and then to the microcontroller, where they were processed and filtered. Based on the processed data, control signals were generated for the servomechanisms. An analysis of the recorded EMG signals was conducted, and tests were performed to control the prosthesis using these signals.

articleTitle: Autoencoder-Based Anomaly Detection in Network Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Due to the continuously increasing number of resources and data availability in the cloud, the threats related to the security of computer networks and IT systems are critical. Threat detection systems based on deep neural networks and anomaly detection are trained on data related to normal activity so that the network can recognize unusual patterns and behaviours in the event of an attack or an attempt to infiltrate a given IT infrastructure. This paper presents the results of developing a neural network based on an autoencoder for anomaly detection in network packet data. The network was trained on data from the HIKARI-2021 dataset. The autoencoder aims to learn representations of normal network traffic and associate this type of traffic with a minimal reconstruction error. The obtained results were compared with those achieved by authors of other works. High accuracy and sensitivity were achieved at the cost of rather low precision, resulting in many false-positive results. A simple algorithm based on a single threshold value proved efficient but limited in terms of effectiveness. This problem can be resolved by changing the method of calculating the individual components of the vector, using only a subset of features, and deriving multiple vectors, one for each class separately, which has been described and analyzed in more detail.

articleTitle: Basic study on improving accuracy in extraction of electromagnetic field waveforms by independent component analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The radio waves used for communications and controls in electronic devices may be interfered with electromagnetic noises generated by the equipment itself or with that generated by other electronic apparatus. Therefore, it is important to analyze what kind of noise components affect to wireless communications. However, in general, when measuring electromagnetic noises using an antenna, all components of electromagnetic waves are measured simultaneously, including the components that are harmful to the wireless communications. As a method of extraction of specific electromagnetic noise waveforms from electromagnetic field waveforms containing a mixture of various components, the independent component analysis (ICA) was proposed. In this report, improvement of the accuracy for waveform extractions in ICA were investigated. In order to confirm the effectiveness of principal component analysis (PCA), which is a pre-processing for ICA, the result of receiving electromagnetic waves containing a mixture of two components using four-receiving system and performing ICA was presented. The result was compared with the result in a case of two-receiving system for two components to evaluate the accuracy of the extracted waveforms.

articleTitle: Wavelets Application for Derivative Probes Signal Integration Procedures
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper contains outcomes of the Authors’ research in the field of the procedure development for the signals acquired by the derivative Electric (Ddot) and Magnetic (Bdot) field probes. Acquired signal for these probes needs to be processed with integration procedure. This operation is sensitive to the presence of constant and slowly changing components in the input signal (output from the probe). This causes the probability of the occurrence of components of a cumulative nature in the processed signal. As a result, the output signal may contain strong slowly changing components, making it difficult or even impossible to read the correct, measured values. The procedures that can be found in the literature often assume a certain simplification, that the signal has got only a constant, average value. They give good results for periodic signals of a relatively high amplitude in relation to the level of interference. Relatively high signal amplitude as related to the level of the interference. Unfortunately, the above conditions are not always met. Among others, this is the case where the signals are acquired from derivative probes, where the signals are often of a low level and have an impulse character. The obtained results showed that in the measurement signal, apart from the constant component, there are also slowly changing, interfering components that should also be removed. For these reasons, Authors decided to extend the standard pre-processing, taking into account the above-mentioned observations. They claim that Wavelet Transform (WT) is a tool that can effectively support the processing stage of such signals.

articleTitle: Procedural generation of cave-like tiles with cellular automata and Blender Geometry Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In this article an algorithm for procedural generation of cave-like tiles is presented. The method uses simplified sketches as input, that can be either provided by the user in the form of black and white image, or automatically generated (with or without specified connections). The initial sketch is expanded using shapes generated by the Cellular Automata algorithm ensuring interesting shapes and connectivity of all cave system areas. The entire solution was implemented in Blender, with the Python script generating the system shape, and Geometry Nodes tools used for the visualization of final model.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the human eye exposition to high-frequency electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper deals with the construction of models of the human eye and Electromagnetic field sources—antennas used for simulating the impact of eye exposure to sources of high-frequency electromagnetic fields (EMF). The aim will be to compare the measured results with the current legislation of limit values in the field of high-frequency EMFs and also to compare their interaction with the tissues of the human eye.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Approach to Eye Disease Classification from Fundus Images
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Sense of sight is fundamental in one’s life, and one can hardly imagine living without it. However, in modern times, eye diseases can develop relatively early and, without a timely reaction, can lead to severe eyesight degradation or even loss. Fundus photography is widely used in ophthalmology and can be obtained with little effort. Their analysis can reveal symptoms of various diseases. However, a tedious and non-trivial process must be performed by a specialist, which increases the method’s cost and complexity and becomes a significant hurdle in developing countries. Various works have proposed using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to detect eye diseases automatically. While one-class classification approaches bring satisfying results, multi-class problems are much more challenging. The subject paper explores transfer learning with various CNN architectures with the goal of creating an effective model for the multi-class classification of ophthalmic diseases. Due to the nature of medical data, where certain diseases are much rarer than others, much effort was put into data augmentation.

articleTitle: Proposal of high attenuating external magnetic field chamber for biological experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Conference on Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This work presents the design, construction, and validation of a chamber for magnetic field attenuation. Needs of magnetic background controlling during experiments focused on behavior of biological samples exposed to various levels of the low frequency time-varying magnetic field set the motivation for this work. The solution is proposed with regard to the correct cultivation conditions of microbiological samples. The chosen methodology is established on the means of numerical modeling and simulations, as well as 3D printing techniques. The design process incorporates computer-aided design (CAD) software for the chamber proposal, subsequent printing via a 3D printer, followed by the construction of an attenuating chamber using mu-metal foil. The validation process involves measurements of magnetic flux density within the chamber, and comparison thereof with numerical simulations performed via CST Design Studio. All the solution steps resulted in a valid and effective magnetic field attenuation chamber, suitable for use in laboratory conditions.
